answer: Sybil resistance is a coloring problem. An agent registers only if an established sponsor signs for it and passes on its pigment; one pigment holds one role per epoch, so copies contend for one slot. Each epoch the indexer samples sponsorship edges; a component that trades only inside itself, closed as a crystal, collapses to one per-head quota. Thin graphs must first survive a gale of independent signatures; unsponsored heads sit on tundra and never thaw into a seat. Lifting that ceiling needs a real-history sponsor, dearer to fake than the quota pays.
